Vs.

full_judgment:
2. Short facts are that the writ petitioners filed writ petition No. 488 of 1994 stating, inter alia, that after partition of India some members of Ansari family, namely, Bashir Ahmed Ansari, Mokter Ahmed Ansari and Peshkar Ahmed Ansari, the three brothers, migrated to the then Pakistan. Late Bashir Ahmed Ansari, father of Ali Akbor Ansari started business in Karachi and the other two brothers, Mokter Ahmed Ansari and Peshkar Ahmed Ansari started their businesses in Dhaka and Chittagong respectively and settled in the then East Pakistan. In 1956 the respondent started his own business in Rajshahi and Chittagong. In 1963 he married a Bengali girl and permanently settled in the then East Pakistan. In 1970 Bashir Ahmed Ansari, the father of the respondent died leaving behind the respondent as his only son and widow Fatema Beugm. After his death his brothers Moktar Ahmed Ansari and Peshker Ahmed Ansari took charge of the business and properties of Ansari Family in the then East and East Pakistan Subsequently both of 'them along with their wives orally gifted all their properties in the then East Pakistan ali Akbar Ansari, the respondent who is the only son of their elder brother. The gift was confirmed by a declaration of gift on 15.01.1971. The respondent along with the members of his family was in peaceful possession of the disputed properties at 426 and 427, Ansari Mansion Enayet Bazar, Batali Road, Chittagong from long before liberation of Bangladesh and also from 15.01.1971 when declaration of gift was made. After liberation of Bangladesh the case properties were declared as abandoned properties by the Government the respondent made several representations to the Board of Management of Abandoned Properties. During the pendency of his applications before the authorities the respondent was evicted from the case properties in the later part of 1979. The case properties were included in the 'k' list in serial Nos. 135 and 136 respectively of the list of abandoned buildings published in the Bangladesh Gazette on the 23rd September, 1986 under Ordinance No. 54 of 1985. The respondent then filed Cases Nos. 1084 of 1987 and 183 of 1988 in respect of holding Nos. 426 and 427 respectively before the Court of Settlement which dismissed both the cases and maintained the inclusion of the properties in the list of abandoned buildings. The respondent then filed Writ Petition Nos. 62 and 63 of 1989 before the High Court Division, Chittagong Bench which were renumbered as Writ Petition Nos. 1497 and 1489 of 1991 respectively in the High Court Division in Dhaka. By judgment and order dated 30.07.1992 the High Court Division declared the enlistment of the case properties in the 'ka' list as illegal and without lawful authority. It was further held that the respondent had proved before the court of Settlement by the oral gift etc. that the case properties were not abandoned properties. The Government petitioners did not prefer any appeal against the judgment and order of the High Court Division and by notification dated 24.05.1993 the Ministry of Works excluded the case properties from the 'ka' list of abandoned buildings. One Abdus Sattar who is a tenant of the disputed properties, later on an allottee filed Review Petition Nos. 4 and 5 of 1993 against the judgment and order of the High Court Division dated 30.07.1992 but the same was rejected by judgment and order dated 12.01.1994 . The Government petitioner also subsequently filed Reviews Petition Nos. 4 and 5 of 1994 against the said judgment and order of the High Court Division dated 30.07.1992 and both the review petitioners were rejected by the High Court Division by judgment and order dated 12.07.1994. The Government petitioner in Civil Petition Nos. 650 and 660 of 1994 and one Md. Amin Chowdhury and others, the petitioners in Civil Petition No. 694 of 1994 preferred petitioner for leave to appeal before the Appellate Division against the rejection of the review applications but those were dismissed. The respondent was not given back his possession of the properties inspite of repeated representations and ultimately they were compelled to file the instant Writ Petition No. 488 of 1994 for getting back vacant possession of the case properties. 

 4. It is on record that the Government petitioner filed other Class Suit No. 109 of 1995 in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge (now joint District Judge) against the respondent No, 1 and others praying for a declaration that by virtue of the alleged oral gift dated 15.01.1971 No title has passed in favour of the respondent and the alleged oral gift is forged. The suit was filed after disposal of the above mentioned writ petitions, review petitions, civil petitions for leave to appeal and after exclusion of the cases properties from the list of abandoned buildings by the government petitioner. The suit was decreed ex-parte on 06.03.1997 and it is not disputed that the ex-parte decree was subsequently set aside in Miscellaneous Case No. 103 of 1997 and the original suit was restored to its file and number. 

 6. This court concurred with the findings of the High Court Division holding, inter alia, that once the disputed properties were released by the Government petitioner from the list of abandoned buildings, the properties had lost the character of abandoned properties and as such the Government petitioner had no locus standi to file the civil suit challenging the validity of the gift made in favour of the respondent after disposal of the writ petitions, review petitions and civil petitions for leave to appeal. The same is the position of tenants lessess in the disputed properties as their interest is derived from the Government and the general observation of the High Court division in the review petition that disputed question of fact can not be decided in the writ petition does not create any right and interest in favour of the Government or the tenants to file a suit before the Civil court to decided title of the case properties specially in face of the fact that the case properties had already been released by the Government from the list of abandoned buildings.
